scope: Recurring cost to manufacture or fulfil one complete internal product at the stated date. Estimates only; no authorisation required.
exclusions: Retail prices, dealer margins, profit and sales tax
Non-recurring product R&D, design masks and launch expenditure
Idle-factory expansion capital beyond the normal depreciation included in wafer costs
policies: Outputs and cost breakdowns are nominal USD for each snapshot date. Internal monetary anchors use June 1978 dollars; CPI escalation is applied once, after real component-price and manufacturing-yield changes.
Use actual dated root product composition and explicitly pinned child versions, without substituting newer hardware.
Keep unknown or out-of-period child revision dates visible as estimation flags; a pin is not a qualification claim.
Use the last day of month/year precision qualification events; June-only releases do not improve June 15 estimates.
Continue estimating a recorded offering through December 1983; this is a hypothetical cost to supply it, not a claim of continuing sales.
AION chip cost includes wafer completion, accepted electrical/grade yield, packaging and final-test yield. Purchased-part estimates include supplier conversion and margin.
Wafer costs assume normal loaded production at the funded planning scale and include raw wafers, fab labour, utilities, maintenance and normal depreciation; do not add factory investment again.
Explicit BOM items remain included even where generic packout descriptions may overlap. No author-approved foundation content is silently deleted.
The low/high range is a sensitivity allowance, not a statistical confidence interval.
Part-specific qualification, supplier contracts and detailed service demand can remain unknown even when a scenario cost is provided.

1978 SRAM capacity assumptions: 160 candidate die, 90% completion, 50% electrical yield and 95% final acceptance. Dollar cost and later improvement are estimates.
Scenario learning curve; dated capability gates come from the story. Later numeric yield/cost values are estimates, not measured claims.
